mainTopic: The treatment of the סוטה: why she is uncovered, the details of her disgrace, who watches her, and the principle of measure for measure (במדה שאדם מודד).
overview: The גמרא explains why the רבנן uncover a סוטה but keep a woman who is being stoned clothed. Uncovering the סוטה warns other women, but stoning is already the greatest warning. רב נחמן adds that even a condemned person must be given a kind death (ברור לו מיתה יפה), learned from 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך.' The רבנן and רבי יהודה both accept this rule. They only disagree about whether shame or pain is worse. The גמרא then works through the lines of the משנה: ugly clothes if black suits her, why her jewelry is removed, why the Egyptian rope is not required, and who may or must watch her. A new משנה teaches מידה כנגד מידה: the סוטה is punished in the same way she sinned. רב יוסף shows that this principle continues today, since heaven brings deaths that match the four deaths of בית דין. A ברייתא then brings פסוקים showing that even small sins are paid back and add up. It begins listing how the סוטה's treatment matches her actions, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Resolving the contradiction in the רבנן's rulings
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן uncover a סוטה to warn other women. At a סקילה there is no need, because the stoning itself is the biggest warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between the רבנן and the רבנן is also not a problem. Here, by a סוטה, what is the reason she is uncovered? Because of the פסוק 'that all women may be warned.' There, by stoning, there is no greater warning than the stoning itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction. The רבנן uncover a סוטה, but they say a woman who is stoned stays clothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Uncovering a סוטה is done to warn other women, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל. A woman being stoned does not need this extra step, because watching the execution is already the strongest possible warning. So the two rulings have different purposes and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction between one ruling of the רבנן and another ruling of theirs
It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
They will be warned / taught a lesson

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult.
phrases.notes: The two rulings are: uncover a סוטה, but keep a woman being stoned clothed. The word 'also' is because the רבי יהודה contradiction was just answered.

phrases.english: Here, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of the סוטה.

phrases.english: Because of "that all women may be chastened."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 23:48

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — אֵין לְךָ יִיסּוּר גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: There, you have no chastening greater than this.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the stoning; 'this' is the stoning itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier answer to the רבי יהודה contradiction, which was given before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different purposes: the reason for uncovering a סוטה does not apply to stoning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seem inconsistent: they uncover a סוטה but not a woman being executed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Uncovering is only to warn others. Stoning already gives the greatest warning, so it is unnecessary there.

steps.title: Why not do both?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't add the shame of uncovering on top of the stoning, to warn even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us do both to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge to the answer it just gave. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If warning others is a good thing, then more warning should be even better. So why not stone her and also uncover her? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us do both to her —
phrases.notes: 'Both' means stoning her and also shaming her by uncovering her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לַעֲבֵיד בַּהּ תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that stoning is warning enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if the stoning is warning enough, adding the shame would only increase the warning.

steps.title: Choose a kind death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, learns from 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' that even a condemned person must be given a kind death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the פסוק says 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose a kind death for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. We may not add extra shame to an execution, because the תורה commands us to give even a condemned person a kind death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of ואהבת לרעך כמוך still applies to someone being put to death. So the death must be as kind as possible, without extra suffering or shame. That is why we don't uncover a woman who is being stoned.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose a kind (literally 'nice') death for him

steps.whatToRemember: ברור לו מיתה יפה: even when בית דין executes someone, it must give that person the kindest death possible, based on ואהבת לרעך כמוך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle comes up across שס whenever the details of an execution are discussed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The verse says: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: Choose for him a good death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק showing that extra shame is not allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could stone her and also uncover her, to warn others even more.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה requires a kind death, so extra shame may not be added.

steps.title: Is רב נחמן's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה, who has the woman stoned unclothed, might reject רב נחמן's principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב נחמן's rule is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree about whether רב נחמן's rule is true. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן keep the woman clothed, which fits a kind death. רבי יהודה has her stoned unclothed, which looks like he ignores the need for a kind death. If so, רב נחמן's rule would be accepted by only one side.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Nachman's teaching is a dispute of tanna'im?
phrases.notes: The תנאים here are the רבנן, who say clothed, and רבי יהודה, who says unclothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the principle in step 3 is accepted by everyone.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה reject the principle of ברור לו מיתה יפה?

steps.title: Everyone agrees; they disagree about shame versus pain
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts רב נחמן's rule. The dispute is only about which is the kinder death: avoiding shame or avoiding physical pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רב נחמן. Here they argue about this: one Sage holds that a person cares more about his shame than his body's pain, and one Sage holds that a person cares more about his body's pain than his shame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both sides want a kind death. They only disagree about what a kind death is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן think shame is worse, so they keep her clothed even though clothing may make the death slower and more painful. רבי יהודה thinks pain is worse, so a quicker death without clothing is kinder, even though it adds shame. Both sides are applying רב נחמן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He cares about it more / it matters more to him

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן and רבי יהודה both follow ברור לו מיתה יפה. They argue only over whether shame or physical pain is worse for a person.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה doesn't care about kindness. He also wants a kind death; he just thinks less pain is kinder than less shame.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: No, everyone holds like Rav Nachman.
And here, they disagree about this:
One Sage holds: his shame matters to him
phrases.notes: This is the רבנן, who keep the woman clothed.

phrases.english: more than the pain of his body,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: צַעְרָא דְגוּפֵיהּ עֲדִיף לֵיהּ
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: the pain of his body matters to him
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who has her stoned unclothed so the death is quicker.

phrases.english: more than his shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רב נחמן's rule is disputed by תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the dispute is about whether a kind death is needed. Really, it is about what makes a death kind.

steps.title: If black clothes suit her, ugly clothes are used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about covering a סוטה dressed in white with black, and quotes a ברייתא: if black looks good on her, she is dressed in ugly clothes instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If she was dressed in white, etc.' It was taught: if black clothes look nice on her, they dress her in ugly clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה and adds a ברייתא that clarifies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to switch her white clothes for black ones. The goal is not the color black itself; the goal is to make her look unattractive. So if black looks good on her, ugly clothes are used instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה
Look nice on her / suit her

phrases.english: If she was dressed in white, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which goes on to say she is then covered in black.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, אִם הָיוּ שְׁחוֹרִים נָאִים לָהּ —
phrases.english: It was taught: if black clothes are becoming to her —
they cover her with ugly clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה מְכוּסָּה לְבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, returning to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The aim is to make the סוטה look unattractive, so if black suits her, ugly clothes are used.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say her jewelry is removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that gold jewelry is taken off the סוטה, and asks why this needs to be said, since she is already being made to look ugly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if she was wearing gold jewelry, it is removed. That is obvious! If the כהן is already making her look ugly, do we even need to be told that her jewelry comes off?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges it as obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן already uncovers her and dresses her in ugly clothes. So of course he would also take off her nice jewelry. The question is why the משנה bothers to spell this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it need to be said?

phrases.english: If she was wearing gold jewelry, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: the jewelry is removed from her.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Now that he is making her look ugly anyway,
do these need to be mentioned?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, הַשְׁתָּא נַוּוֹלֵי מְנַוֵּויל לַהּ, הָנֵי מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the black clothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that gold jewelry is removed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since she is already being made ugly, removing jewelry seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: Jewelry might seem to add to her shame
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one might think leaving the jewelry on would shame her even more, like a naked person wearing shoes. So the משנה teaches that it is removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: with the jewelry on, she is shamed even more, just as people say, 'Stripped, naked, and wearing shoes.' So the משנה teaches us that the jewelry is removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's line is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a real reason to think the jewelry should stay: fancy items on an uncovered person can make her look even more embarrassing. The משנה rules out that idea and says the jewelry is removed anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Stripped, naked, and wearing shoes (a saying)

phrases.english: You might have said:
with these on, she has more shame,
as people say:
Stripped, naked, and wearing shoes.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that the משנה's line is obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable opposite assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving the jewelry on would shame her even more, so it should stay on.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that the jewelry is removed.

steps.title: Is the Egyptian rope required?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב הונא whether the כהן must use specifically an Egyptian rope. It depends on why the rope is used: just to hold up her clothes, or as a measure-for-measure punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: afterward he brings a rope. רבי אבא asked רב הונא: Is the Egyptian rope required for a סוטה? Is it there only so her clothes won't fall off, in which case even a small ribbon is enough? Or is it because of what was taught: 'She dressed up for him with a ribbon, so the כהן brings an Egyptian rope and ties it above her chest,' in which case the Egyptian rope is required?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא asks a real question about the rope in the משנה, with two possible sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rope's only job is practical, holding up her clothes, any string would do. If it is a measure-for-measure response to her dressing up with a pretty ribbon, then the rough Egyptian rope itself matters. The answer depends on which reason is the real one.

keyTerms.meaning: Required, so that without it the ceremony doesn't work

phrases.english: And afterward he brings a rope, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה again: the כהן ties a rope on her.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba asked Rav Huna:
Is the Egyptian rope required for a sotah?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁמְטוּ בְּגָדֶיהָ מֵעָלֶיהָ הוּא,
phrases.english: Is it there so her clothes won't fall off her,
and then even a small ribbon would be enough,
or maybe it is because of what the Master said:
'She dressed up for him with a ribbon,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the man she was secluded with.

phrases.english: therefore the kohen brings an Egyptian rope
and ties it on her above her chest'
so it is required?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, about the rope.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Egyptian rope specifically is required, based on whether its purpose is practical or a measure-for-measure punishment.

steps.title: The rope is only to hold up her clothes
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers from a ברייתא that the rope is tied so her clothes won't fall off, so the Egyptian rope itself is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: You already learned this: 'Afterward he brings an Egyptian rope and ties it on her above her chest, so that her clothes won't fall off her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רבי אבא's question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason for the rope: so her clothes stay on. That is the practical reason, the first side of the question. So any tie would work, and the Egyptian rope is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a ברייתא)
So that they won't slip off

steps.whatToRemember: The rope's purpose is to hold up her clothes, so the specific Egyptian rope is not required.

phrases.english: He said to him: You already learned it:
And afterward he brings an Egyptian rope
and ties it on her above her chest,
so that her clothes won't fall off her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, תְּנֵיתוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא says the rope is to keep her clothes from falling, so the Egyptian rope is not required.

steps.title: Contradiction in the משנה: may men watch her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה first says anyone may watch her, meaning men and women, but then says all women may watch her, implying men may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: anyone who wants to watch her may watch. This line contradicts itself. You say anyone who wants may watch, so it seems men and women are the same. But then it teaches: all women are allowed to watch her. That means women yes, men no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two lines of the same משנה. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line sounds open to everyone, men included. The later line singles out women, which suggests men are not allowed. Both cannot be read simply, so the גמרא needs to explain how they fit.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the סוטה herself. It is about two lines of the same משנה that seem to disagree about who may watch.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הָרוֹצֶה לִרְאוֹת בָּהּ יִרְאֶה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And anyone who wants to watch her may watch, etc.
This itself is difficult.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִרְאוֹת בָּהּ רוֹאֶה,
phrases.english: You said: Anyone who wants to watch her may watch,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא גַּבְרֵי וְלָא שְׁנָא נְשֵׁי,
phrases.english: so apparently men and women are the same,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים מוּתָּרוֹת לִרְאוֹתָהּ:
phrases.english: and then it teaches: All women are allowed to watch her:
women, yes; men, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and finds an internal contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's lines about who may watch the סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first line includes men, but the later line implies only women may watch.

steps.title: אביי limits the first line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the contradiction by reading the first line of the משנה, 'anyone may watch,' as referring only to women, so men may not watch and the two lines no longer clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Explain the first line as talking about one specific group.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a first answer to the contradiction from Step 11 by saying the first line of the משנה is not really about everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that 'anyone may watch' seems to include men, but 'all women may watch' seems to exclude them. אביי reads the first line as meaning 'any woman may watch.' Then both lines agree that men may not watch.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'men'; here אביי uses the contrast to limit the first line to women only

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Explain it as referring to [women only].
phrases.notes: אביי means the first line, 'anyone may watch,' is only about women, so men may not watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי תרגמה אנשים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of one clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first line means every single person, including men.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first line refers only to women, so men may not watch, and it does not contradict the second line.

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי's limitation
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה clearly says 'anyone who wants to watch,' which cannot be limited to one group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But the משנה says 'anyone who wants to watch her may watch'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's answer, saying the words of the משנה do not allow that limitation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'anyone' (כל הרוצה) is completely open and general. You cannot shrink it to one group without going against the plain wording, so אביי's answer does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, (introduces a challenge from the text)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But [the משנה says] 'anyone who wants
to watch her may watch'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא והא כל הרוצה לראות בה רואה קתני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'anyone' is fully general and cannot be limited to one group.

steps.title: רבא's answer: anyone may watch, but women must watch
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that both men and women are allowed to watch, and the second line adds that women are obligated to watch, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Anyone who wants to watch her may watch, men and women alike. And women are obligated to watch her, as the פסוק says: 'So that all the women will be warned and not act like your immorality.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer: the two lines of the משנה are not talking about the same thing, so they don't contradict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line is about permission: anyone, men or women, may watch. The second line is about obligation: women must watch, so they will learn a lesson. The פסוק in יחזקאל shows that the purpose is to warn women.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will be warned / taught a lesson

steps.whatToRemember: The first line of the משנה gives permission to everyone; the second line puts an obligation on women. So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Anyone who wants to watch her may watch,
no difference if they are men
and no difference if they are women.
And women are obligated to watch her,
as it says: 'And all the women will be warned
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 23:48

phrases.english: and not act like your immorality.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא כל הרוצה לראות בה רואה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's answer, רבא offers a new resolution to the contradiction in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two different kinds of rule (permission vs. obligation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second line means only women may watch, which would exclude men.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone may watch; the second line only adds that women are required to watch.

steps.title: New משנה: a person is punished the way he sinned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches the rule of measure for measure and shows how each part of the סוטה's punishment matches her sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With the measure a person uses, he is measured. She dressed herself up for sin, so God made her look ugly. She exposed herself for sin, so God exposed her. She began the sin with the thigh and then the belly, so the thigh is struck first and then the belly, and the rest of the body does not escape.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching that God punishes a person in a way that matches what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail of the סוטה's treatment mirrors her actions: dressing up leads to being made ugly, exposing herself leads to being exposed. Even the order in which the bitter water affects her body matches the order of her sin.

keyTerms.meaning: With the measure a person measures (measure for measure)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why all the earlier details of the סוטה procedure (messing her hair, tearing her clothes) are done: they are measure-for-measure responses to her actions.

phrases.english: MISHNA: With the measure that a person measures —
with it they measure him.
She adorned herself for a sin —
God made her ugly.
She exposed herself for a sin —
God exposed her.
With the thigh she began the sin first
and afterward the belly —
therefore the thigh is struck first
and afterward the belly,
and the rest of the whole body does not escape.

steps.triggerLanguage: במדה שאדם מודד בה מודדין לו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic: the principle behind the punishments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God punishes a person measure for measure, matching the punishment to the sin.

steps.title: רב יוסף: measure-for-measure punishment never stopped
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that even though בית דין punishments have stopped, God's measure-for-measure punishment still continues.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יוסף said: Even though the measure has stopped, 'with the measure' has not stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה with a teaching from רב יוסף about the measure-for-measure rule today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today there is no בית דין with the power to give death penalties, so that 'measure' has ended. But God still punishes people in a way that matches their sins, so the principle of the משנה still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Has stopped / is no longer in effect

steps.whatToRemember: Human court punishments may stop, but God's measure-for-measure justice never stops.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yosef said:
Even though the measure has stopped,
phrases.notes: He means the punishments carried out by בית דין, which no longer happen today.

phrases.english: 'with the measure' has not stopped.
phrases.notes: He means God's matching of punishment to sin, using the משנה's own words 'with the measure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף אף על גב דמדה בטילה במדה לא בטיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the principle stated in the משנה in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's measure-for-measure punishment continues even after בית דין punishments ended.

steps.title: The source: the four deaths did not stop
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, together with a teaching of רבי חייא, says that even after the סנהדרין stopped, the four deaths of בית דין did not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said, and רבי חייא taught the same: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, even though the סנהדרין stopped, the four types of death did not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind רב יוסף's statement from Step 16. It quotes a teaching that the four deaths of בית דין 'did not stop' even after the סנהדרין ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, רב יוסף said that measure-for-measure punishment still continues. Here is his proof: a teaching that the four deaths continue even without a סנהדרין. The wording sounds strange, and the גמרא is about to question it.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court that could judge cases of the death penalty
The four deaths of בית דין: stoning, burning, the sword, and strangling
'And so taught': a ברייתא that says the same thing

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef said,
and so Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
From the day the Temple was destroyed,
even though the Sanhedrin stopped,
the four types of death did not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that backs up רב יוסף's statement in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that measure-for-measure punishment continues even without בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי חייא that the four deaths did not stop after the חורבן

steps.title: But the four deaths did stop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: of course the four deaths stopped, since no court carries them out anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they did stop!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the teaching it just quoted. Today no בית דין executes anyone, so how can we say the four deaths 'did not stop'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the teaching says something that is plainly not true. Without a סנהדרין, nobody is put to death by בית דין. The challenge pushes us to find a better reading of the words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely…': a word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But they did stop!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּטְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain wording of the teaching in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'the four deaths did not stop'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a סנהדרין, no court carries out the death penalty, so the four deaths really did stop.

steps.title: The law of the four deaths did not stop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching means the law of the four deaths continues, not that בית דין carries them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: the law of the four deaths did not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. The teaching means that the 'law' of the four deaths continues, even though no court carries it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the teaching is about God, not about בית דין. A person who deserves one of the four deaths still gets a death that matches it, sent by heaven. This is exactly רב יוסף's point that measure for measure continues.
steps.whatToRemember: The four deaths still happen today. They do not come through בית דין. God brings a matching death on the person who deserves it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דִּין אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת לֹא בָּטְלוּ.
phrases.english: Rather: the law of the four deaths did not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דִּין אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת לֹא בָּטְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 by reading the teaching more carefully.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: 'the four deaths' means 'the law of the four deaths'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching meant that בית דין still carries out the four deaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judgment of the four deaths continues through God, who brings a matching death.

steps.title: How each of the four deaths still happens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists how a person who deserves each of the four deaths still dies in a matching way.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who deserves stoning either falls from a roof or a wild animal mauls him. One who deserves burning either falls into a fire or a snake bites him. One who deserves the sword either is handed over to the government or robbers attack him. One who deserves strangling either drowns in a river or dies of a throat disease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what 'the law of the four deaths' means in practice. For each death of בית דין, it gives two kinds of death that look like it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair matches the court's death. A fall or a mauling breaks the bones, like stoning. Fire or a burning snakebite is like burning. Being killed by the government or by robbers is like the sword. Drowning or a disease that closes the throat is like strangling.

keyTerms.meaning: A disease that closes up the throat (diphtheria)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that measure for measure is not a vague idea. Heaven's punishment really copies the shape of the punishment the person deserved.

phrases.english: One who deserves stoning —
either falls from a roof,
or a wild animal mauls him.
One who deserves burning —
either falls into a fire,
or a snake bites him.
phrases.notes: A snakebite burns, so it is like the death of burning.

phrases.english: One who deserves the sword —
either is handed over to the government,
or robbers attack him.
One who deserves strangling —
either drowns in a river,
or dies of a throat disease.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב סְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'law of the four deaths' from Step 19 with real examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For each of the four deaths, heaven brings a matching death: falling or mauling for stoning, fire or snakebite for burning, government or robbers for the sword, drowning or throat disease for strangling.

steps.title: A פסוק for measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי brings a פסוק showing that a person is measured with the same measure he uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי used to say: From where do we know that with the measure a person measures, he is measured? As it says: 'With a סאה, when you send her away, you contend with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a source in a פסוק for measure for measure. רבי reads the word 'בסאסאה' as 'with a סאה,' a unit of measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17–20 showed that measure for measure works. Now we get a פסוק as its source. The 'סאה' is the measure the sinner used, and God 'contends' with him, meaning punishes him, using that same measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure; here, the way a person acts
A large unit for measuring dry goods
You contend with her (you punish her)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi used to say:
From where do we know that with the measure a person measures,
he is measured with it?
As it says: 'With a se'a, when you send her away, you contend with her.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:8. רבי hears 'בסאסאה' as 'בסאה,' with a סאה measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּמִדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד בָּהּ מוֹדְדִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that measure for measure still works, the גמרא brings its source in a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is punished with the same measure he used, learned from 'בסאסאה' in ישעיהו.

steps.title: What about smaller measures?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: the פסוק speaks of a big סאה, so how do we know the rule also covers smaller measures?
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about a סאה. From where do we include a half-סאה and half of that, a קב and a half-קב, a quarter-קב and half of that, an eighth-קב and an עוכלא? From where?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question about the פסוק it just used. A סאה is a big measure, so the פסוק might only be talking about big sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question lists smaller and smaller measures, all the way down to a tiny עוכלא. It wants to know whether small sins are also paid back measure for measure. This sets up the next step, which brings another פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only know…': the פסוק seems to teach only this
A smaller measure, one-sixth of a סאה
A tiny measure, one thirty-second of a קב

phrases.english: I only know about a se'a;
from where do we include a tarkav and a half-tarkav,
a kav and a half-kav,
a quarter-kav and half a quarter-kav,
an eighth-kav and an ukla, from where?
phrases.notes: Each measure here is smaller than the one before. The idea is smaller and smaller sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא סְאָה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far the פסוק in Step 21 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that measure for measure applies even to smaller measures, meaning smaller sins.

steps.title: Every measure counts, even a small one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from another פסוק that every 'סאון' is punished, so even small measures are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'For every boot stamped with fierceness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a second פסוק. The word 'כל,' every, together with 'סאון,' which רבי reads as a small סאה, teaches that every measure is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק spoke only of a full סאה. This פסוק says 'every סאון,' so even the smallest measure, meaning even a small sin, is paid back in kind. Measure for measure applies to sins of every size.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק says': brings the answer from a פסוק
Here read as a small סאה measure

steps.whatToRemember: Measure for measure applies to every sin, big or small. The first פסוק (a סאה) teaches the rule, and the second (every סאון) stretches it down to the smallest measure.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי כׇּל סְאוֹן סֹאֵן בְּרַעַשׁ״.
phrases.english: The verse says: 'For every boot stamped with fierceness.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:4. The plain meaning of 'סאון' is a soldier's boot, but רבי reads it as a small סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי כׇּל סְאוֹן סֹאֵן בְּרַעַשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Every סאון' includes even small measures, so small sins are also paid back measure for measure.

steps.title: How do we know small amounts add up to a big total?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a source that every single פרוטה joins together into one large total.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that each and every פרוטה joins together into a big total?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks one more question about the rule of measure for measure. It wants a source that even tiny amounts are added together in the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 showed that even small measures are punished. Now the ברייתא goes one step further: small amounts are not only counted, they also pile up together. So a person who is not punished right away for a small sin should not think it was forgotten.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know
The smallest coin; here, a tiny amount of wrongdoing
A big total, a large account

phrases.english: And from where do we know that each and every פרוטה
joins together into a big total?
phrases.notes: The coins stand for small sins. Even if each one gets no punishment right away, they all count toward one big final account.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁכׇּל פְּרוּטָה וּפְרוּטָה מִצְטָרֶפֶת לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 23: small measures are not only punished, they also add up together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that small separate wrongdoings combine into one large account.

steps.title: The פסוק: one by one to find the total
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with the פסוק in קהלת, 'one to one, to find the total.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Adding one to one, to find the total.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one to one' show items being added together one at a time. 'To find the total' shows that in the end they make up one complete sum. So every small sin is added in until the full account is reached.

keyTerms.meaning: One to one, adding item after item

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Adding one to one, to find the total."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:27

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אַחַת לְאַחַת לִמְצֹא חֶשְׁבּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'one to one, to find the total' shows that small items are added together into a full account.
steps.whatToRemember: The general rule is now complete: a person is measured by his own measure, even small measures count, and small amounts all add up into one big total.

steps.title: The סוטה is also measured by her own measure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the rule of measure for measure to the סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so we find with a סוטה: with the measure she measured, they measured her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings the general rule back to our topic, the סוטה. This line sets up the list of examples that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא taught a general rule about how people are punished. Here it states that the treatment of the סוטה follows the same rule. The details come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife suspected of being with another man after her husband warned her

phrases.english: And so we find with a סוטה,
that with the measure she measured,
with it they measured her:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בַּסּוֹטָה, שֶׁבַּמִּדָּה שֶׁמָּדְדָה בָּהּ מָדְדוּ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general rule of measure for measure back to the סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treatment of the סוטה matches what she did.

steps.title: Each thing she did is matched by what the כהן does
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists matching pairs: standing at her door matches standing at שער נקנור, her pretty scarves match losing her head covering, and her made-up face begins the next pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: She stood at the entrance of her house to be seen by him, so the כהן stands her at שער נקנור and shows her shame to everyone. She spread pretty scarves on her head for him, so the כהן takes the covering off her head and puts it under her feet. She made up her face for him, so...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives examples of how each act of the סוטה is matched by what is done to her in the בית המקדש. The last example continues past this part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair follows one pattern: 'she did X for him, so the כהן does the matching thing.' She showed herself off in public, so she is shamed in public. She made her head look beautiful, so her head covering is removed and put down low.

keyTerms.meaning: The Nikanor gate in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Every 'him' (לו) here means the other man she was trying to attract, not her husband and not the כהן.

phrases.english: She stood at the entrance of her house
to be seen by him,
therefore a כהן stands her
at the Nikanor gate
and shows her shame to everyone.
She spread pretty scarves for him
on her head,
therefore a כהן takes the head covering
off her head and puts it under her feet.
She made up her face for him,
therefore...

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא עָמְדָה עַל פֶּתַח בֵּיתָהּ לֵירָאוֹת לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the detailed examples of the rule stated in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each act the סוטה did to attract the other man is matched by a shaming act the כהן does to her.
